sources.title: Maṇimēkalai · English translation by Kausalya Hart
sources.edition: Project Madurai Unicode text; English translation by Kausalya Hart
sources.locator: Prologue; cantos 1, 5, 9, 10, and 11 (Hart canto and line numbering)

claims.subject: tamil_chembiyan
claims.summary: After Agastya advises him to hold the festival, Chembiyan invites Indra to Pukār for the twenty-eight-day celebration.
claims.speaker: Narrator
claims.note: Passage-level relationship in Hart’s translation; this is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_kaveri
claims.summary: The personified Kāviri worships Sambāpathi after Agastya tells her to do so.
claims.speaker: Narrator
claims.note: The poem personifies Kāviri; this claim concerns the goddess/river as an acting narrative figure.

claims.subject: tamil_goddess_manimekalai
claims.summary: The goddess Maṇimēkalai carries the heroine to Maṇipallavam.
claims.speaker: Narrator
claims.note: The goddess and the heroine are separate characters despite sharing a name.

claims.subject: tamil_goddess_manimekalai
claims.summary: The goddess appears before Sutamati/Sudhamathi after taking the heroine away.
claims.speaker: Narrator
claims.note: The goddess and the heroine are separate characters despite sharing a name.

claims.subject: tamil_bhudam_pukar
claims.summary: The Pukār guardian Bhūdam is described as protecting the city and threatening to destroy it if the Indra festival is neglected.
claims.speaker: Narrator
claims.note: The Tamil text calls this a guardian Bhūdam; it is treated as a named narrative being, not a historical person.

claims.subject: tamil_kama
claims.summary: The passage attributes the heroine’s lovely body to Kāma, described as formless and carrying five flower arrows.
claims.speaker: Narrator
claims.note: Passage-level relationship in Hart’s translation; this is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_murugan
claims.summary: Sudhamathi compares the prince’s handsome body to Murugan, who split Kurugu mountain.
claims.speaker: Sudhamathi in quoted speech
claims.note: Passage-level relationship in Hart’s translation; this is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_brahmadarman
claims.summary: Brahmadarman is identified as the brother-in-law of Adipathi, king of Purva Desam in Kāndāram.
claims.speaker: Manimekalai recounting what the Buddha Peedihai told her
claims.note: Passage-level relationship in Hart’s translation; this is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_brahmadarman
claims.summary: The Buddha Peedihai warns Brahmadarman that Nāganāḍu will be destroyed by an earthquake.
claims.speaker: Manimekalai recounting what the Buddha Peedihai told her
claims.note: Passage-level relationship in Hart’s translation; this is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_brahmadarman
claims.summary: After the warning, Brahmadarman orders the people to leave and travels north with his army to Avanthi.
claims.speaker: Manimekalai recounting what the Buddha Peedihai told her
claims.note: Passage-level relationship in Hart’s translation; this is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_ravivarman
claims.summary: The heroine says she was born as Lakshmi to Amudapathi, queen of Ravivarman.
claims.speaker: Manimekalai
claims.note: Passage-level relationship in Hart’s translation; this is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_lakshmi_past
claims.summary: The heroine identifies her former birth as Lakshmi, daughter of Queen Amudapathi.
claims.speaker: Manimekalai
claims.note: The claim is the heroine’s account of a previous birth within the epic.

claims.subject: tamil_ragulan
claims.summary: Rāgulan is said to have been born to Neelapathi, daughter of Shripathi.
claims.speaker: Manimekalai recounting the Buddha Peedihai’s account
claims.note: Passage-level relationship in Hart’s translation; this is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_neelapathi
claims.summary: Neelapathi is identified as the daughter of Shripathi, king of Chitipuram.
claims.speaker: Manimekalai recounting the Buddha Peedihai’s account
claims.note: Passage-level relationship in Hart’s translation; this is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_lakshmi_past
claims.summary: In her narrated former birth as Lakshmi, the heroine says she married Rāgulan.
claims.speaker: Manimekalai
claims.note: The claim is the heroine’s account of a previous birth within the epic.

claims.subject: tamil_goddess_manimekalai
claims.summary: The Buddha Peedihai’s message, repeated by the heroine, says she would be born in Thavākkali Mudur as Kavera Kanni.
claims.speaker: Manimekalai recounting what the Buddha Peedihai told her
claims.note: Hart’s translation attributes the prediction to the Buddha Peedihai; the goddess Maṇimēkalai is said to bring Kavera Kanni to the island.

claims.subject: tamil_goddess_manimekalai
claims.summary: The heroine recounts the prediction that the goddess Maṇimēkalai would take Kavera Kanni to a southern island.
claims.speaker: Manimekalai recounting what the Buddha Peedihai told her
claims.note: Kavera Kanni is kept distinct from the heroine’s current and previous-birth names.

claims.subject: tamil_goddess_manimekalai
claims.summary: The goddess Maṇimēkalai tells the heroine that her previous-birth name was Lakshmi.
claims.speaker: Narrator
claims.note: Passage-level relationship in Hart’s translation; this is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_sadhu_chakran
claims.summary: As Lakshmi, the heroine and Rāgulan offer food and water to the arriving sage Sādhu Chakran.
claims.speaker: Goddess Maṇimēkalai in quoted speech
claims.note: This is the goddess’s narration of the heroine’s previous birth.

claims.subject: tamil_ragulan
claims.summary: The goddess recalls Rāgulan as Lakshmi’s husband in the heroine’s previous birth.
claims.speaker: Goddess Maṇimēkalai in quoted speech
claims.note: This is the goddess’s narration of the heroine’s previous birth.

claims.subject: tamil_udayakumaran
claims.summary: The goddess identifies the prince Udayakumaran as the heroine’s former husband Rāgulan reborn.
claims.speaker: Goddess Maṇimēkalai in quoted speech
claims.note: The identification is a rebirth claim made within the epic narrative.

claims.subject: tamil_thuchayan
claims.summary: The goddess says Thārai was one of the elder sisters of the heroine and was married to Thuchayan, king of Aṅganāṭu.
claims.speaker: Goddess Maṇimēkalai in quoted speech
claims.note: Passage-level relationship in Hart’s translation; this is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_thuchayan
claims.summary: The goddess says Vīrai was one of the heroine’s elder sisters and was married to Thuchayan, king of Aṅganāṭu.
claims.speaker: Goddess Maṇimēkalai in quoted speech
claims.note: Passage-level relationship in Hart’s translation; this is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_aravanar
claims.summary: In the narrated former birth, Aravanar tells the heroine about the Buddha’s footprints on the hill and invites her to worship there.
claims.speaker: Goddess Maṇimēkalai in quoted speech
claims.note: The episode is told by the goddess as part of the heroine’s previous-birth account.

claims.subject: tamil_tharai
claims.summary: The goddess says Thārai was born as Mādhavi in the present birth.
claims.speaker: Goddess Maṇimēkalai in quoted speech
claims.note: Rebirth relationship stated within the epic narrative.

claims.subject: tamil_veerai
claims.summary: The goddess says Vīrai was born as Sudhamathi in the present birth.
claims.speaker: Goddess Maṇimēkalai in quoted speech
claims.note: Rebirth relationship stated within the epic narrative.

claims.subject: tamil_apputhiran
claims.summary: Deepathilahai explains that Āputhiran placed the inexhaustible Amudhasurabhi in Gomuki pond so it would appear on the Buddha’s birthday.
claims.speaker: Deepathilahai in quoted speech
claims.note: Passage-level relationship in Hart’s translation; this is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: indra
claims.summary: Deepathilahai says Indra made abundant rain after becoming angry at Āputhiran, leaving him with no one to feed.
claims.speaker: Deepathilahai in quoted speech
claims.note: Passage-level relationship in Hart’s translation; this is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_sadhu_chakran
claims.summary: The heroine recalls that Sādhu Chakran once fed her, in a previous birth, and associates that merit with receiving the food-giving vessel.
claims.speaker: Manimekalai
claims.note: The claim is the heroine’s account of a prior-life event, not an independent historical assertion.
